title: Your First Weekend at Bowdoin College, Shared as Cards
description: A guide to the essential first-weekend experiences for new Bowdoin students, from orientation traditions to exploring the Maine coast.

cards.title: Kick Off Arrival Day
cards.subtitle: Check-in and OneCard Pickup
cards.notes: Start your journey by picking up your OneCard and room keys at the field house before moving into your first-year brick dormitory.
cards.short_summary: The official starting point for new students to collect essentials and begin move-in.
cards.evidence_claim: Arrival Day for new students includes check-in and OneCard pickup at Farley Field House from 8:30 A.M. to 1:30 P.M.
cards.access_notes: Open to incoming students and families during scheduled orientation hours.

cards.title: Join Your Orientation Trip
cards.subtitle: Small-Group Maine Adventures
cards.notes: Bond with classmates on a device-free trip, ranging from backpacking in the mountains to community service in local towns.
cards.short_summary: A signature Bowdoin tradition involving small-group excursions across Maine to build community.
cards.evidence_claim: Orientation Trips are a device-free, small-group experience designed to help new students connect and explore the Maine landscape.
cards.access_notes: Required for all first-year students; locations vary by specific trip assignment.

cards.title: Explore the Maine Coast
cards.subtitle: Harpswell Sound Research Station
cards.notes: Visit Bowdoin's 118-acre coastal campus for hiking, sailing, or watercolor painting during orientation weekend.
cards.short_summary: A coastal facility used for research and orientation trips, featuring 2.5 miles of shoreline.
cards.evidence_claim: The Schiller Coastal Studies Center hosts orientation trips involving sailing, hiking, and camping on Harpswell Sound.
cards.access_notes: Accessible via college-provided transportation during orientation or by personal vehicle.

cards.title: Dine at Thorne Hall
cards.subtitle: Campus Dining Hub
cards.notes: Enjoy a meal in the largest dining hall, known for its high ceilings and views of the surrounding pine trees.
cards.short_summary: The primary dining location on campus, frequently cited for high-quality collegiate food.
cards.evidence_claim: Thorne Hall is the largest dining hall at Bowdoin and serves brunch and dinner on weekends.
cards.access_notes: Weekend brunch is served 11:00 AM to 1:30 PM; dinner 5:00 PM to 7:30 PM.

cards.title: Visit the Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: Historic Walker Art Building
cards.notes: Walk through the glass pavilion to see a world-class collection ranging from ancient artifacts to modern masterpieces.
cards.short_summary: A free campus museum housing over 20,000 works of art in a landmark neo-Renaissance building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bowdoin College Museum of Art is open to the public and admission is always free.
cards.access_notes: Open Sunday 1:00 PM to 5:00 PM; closed Mondays.

cards.title: Late Night Super Snack
cards.subtitle: Weekend Comfort Food
cards.notes: Head to Thorne Hall late at night for nachos and cookies, a favorite weekend social tradition for students.
cards.short_summary: A popular late-night dining event featuring comfort food and music.
cards.evidence_claim: Super Snack occurs at Thorne Hall Thursday to Saturday nights from 10:00 PM to 1:00 AM.
cards.source_title: The insider's guide to dining at Bowdoin
cards.access_notes: Late-night hours: 10:00 PM to 1:00 AM, Thursday through Saturday.

cards.title: Practice the Bowdoin Hello
cards.subtitle: Campus Greeting Tradition
cards.notes: Adopt the friendly habit of greeting everyone you pass on the campus paths, a tradition dating back decades.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing campus culture of friendliness where students greet one another while walking.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bowdoin Hello is an ongoing tradition where students greet each other on campus paths.
cards.access_notes: Occurs naturally throughout the campus at all times.

cards.title: Study in Hubbard Hall
cards.subtitle: Quiet Academic Space
cards.notes: Find a quiet corner in the historic reading room to get a head start on your first-week readings.
cards.short_summary: A grand, quiet study space located in one of the campus's most historic buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hubbard Hall Reading Room is a designated quiet study space available for students.
cards.source_title: A New Chapter: Enter the Hubbard Hall Reading Room | Bowdoin College
cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; check current schedule for weekend access.

cards.title: Relax at Smith Union
cards.subtitle: Student Activity Center
cards.notes: Visit the lower level for snacks at Bowdoin Express or the upper level for a smoothie at The Café.
cards.short_summary: The central hub for student life, housing the bookstore, mail center, and multiple dining options.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith Union houses The Café, Jack Magee's Grill, and the Bowdoin Express convenience store.
cards.access_notes: Bowdoin Express is open until midnight on weekends.

cards.title: Gather at Moulton Union
cards.subtitle: Main Lounge Events
cards.notes: Check the Main Lounge for orientation events or meet up with new friends in this central campus landmark.
cards.short_summary: A historic building used for dining and various student orientation programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Moulton Union's Main Lounge is a frequent site for orientation meetings and student gatherings.
cards.access_notes: Open daily; specific event times vary by orientation schedule.
